items.lesson_concept: Republic Act No. 10173 is the comprehensive privacy law of the Philippines, officially known as the Data Privacy Act of 2012[cite: 1].
items.question_text: What is the official short title of Republic Act No. 10173?
items.correct_answer: Data Privacy Act of 2012
items.explanation: Republic Act No. 10173 is formally titled the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (DPA)[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: The NPC stands for the National Privacy Commission, which is the independent regulatory body created to administer the Data Privacy Act[cite: 1].
items.question_text: In the context of the Philippine Data Privacy Act, what does the acronym 'NPC' stand for?
items.correct_answer: National Privacy Commission
items.explanation: The National Privacy Commission (NPC) was established to implement and enforce the provisions of the Data Privacy Act[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: The National Privacy Commission operates as an independent body, but it is attached to the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) for policy and program coordination[cite: 1].
items.question_text: To which government department is the National Privacy Commission (NPC) attached for policy and program coordination?
options: Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT)
Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG)
items.correct_answer: Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT)
items.explanation: Under the law, the NPC is attached to the DICT strictly for the purpose of policy and program coordination[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: Privacy is a fundamental human right recognized in the 1987 Philippine Constitution, primarily protected under Article III, which is known as the Bill of Rights[cite: 1].
items.question_text: Which Article of the 1987 Philippine Constitution contains the Bill of Rights that protects a citizen's right to privacy?
items.correct_answer: Article III
items.explanation: Article III of the 1987 Philippine Constitution is the Bill of Rights, which houses the primary constitutional protections for privacy[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: Article III, Section 3 of the Philippine Constitution explicitly guarantees that the 'privacy of communication and correspondence shall be inviolable'[cite: 1].
items.question_text: Which specific section of the Bill of Rights explicitly guarantees the inviolability of the privacy of communication and correspondence?
items.correct_answer: Article III, Section 3
items.explanation: Article III, Section 3 expressly protects the privacy of communication and correspondence[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: Article III, Section 2 of the Philippine Constitution protects individuals against unreasonable searches and seizures of their papers and effects[cite: 1].
items.question_text: Which section of the Bill of Rights protects individuals against unreasonable searches and seizures?
items.correct_answer: Article III, Section 2
items.explanation: Article III, Section 2 deals with protecting citizens against unreasonable searches and seizures of their person, houses, papers, and effects[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: The Data Privacy Act seeks to balance two main interests: protecting the fundamental right to privacy and ensuring the free flow of information to promote innovation and growth[cite: 1].
items.question_text: According to the Declaration of Policy of the DPA, the State protects the fundamental right to privacy while simultaneously ensuring what?
options: The free flow of information to promote innovation and growth
The absolute secrecy of government documents
The monitoring of all internet traffic
items.correct_answer: The free flow of information to promote innovation and growth
items.explanation: The DPA balances privacy protections with the need to ensure the free flow of information to foster economic innovation and growth[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: The Data Privacy Act applies to the processing of personal information by any natural person (individuals) and juridical person (organizations, companies)[cite: 1].
items.question_text: Who is covered by the regulations of the Data Privacy Act when processing personal data?
options: Any natural and juridical person involved in personal information processing
Only businesses with more than 1,000 employees
items.correct_answer: Any natural and juridical person involved in personal information processing
items.explanation: The DPA is broad in scope and applies to any natural and juridical person involved in personal information processing in both public and private sectors[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: The DPA applies to the processing of all types of personal information, covering both automated digital equipment and structured manual filing systems (paper records)[cite: 1].
items.question_text: Does the Data Privacy Act apply to physical, paper-based records?
options: Yes, it applies to all types of personal information, including structured manual filing systems.
No, it only applies to digital computer databases.
No, physical papers are exempt from the law.
Yes, but only if the paper records belong to the government.
items.correct_answer: Yes, it applies to all types of personal information, including structured manual filing systems.
items.explanation: The DPA protects personal information regardless of its format, covering both digital records and structured physical files[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: Extraterritorial application means the DPA can apply to acts done outside the Philippines if they relate to the personal information of Philippine citizens or residents[cite: 1].
items.question_text: What does the 'extraterritorial application' of the Data Privacy Act mean?
options: It only applies to foreigners visiting the Philippines.
It can apply to entities outside the Philippines if they process the data of Philippine citizens or residents.
It exempts all international companies from following the law.
It allows the NPC to arrest foreign nationals globally.
items.correct_answer: It can apply to entities outside the Philippines if they process the data of Philippine citizens or residents.
items.explanation: The DPA applies extraterritorially, meaning it reaches beyond Philippine borders to protect the data of its citizens and residents[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: To execute its mandate, the NPC is headed by one (1) Privacy Commissioner who serves as the Chairman, and two (2) Deputy Privacy Commissioners[cite: 1].
items.question_text: What is the basic leadership composition of the National Privacy Commission?
options: One (1) Director and four (4) Board Members
One (1) Privacy Commissioner and two (2) Deputy Privacy Commissioners
items.correct_answer: One (1) Privacy Commissioner and two (2) Deputy Privacy Commissioners
items.explanation: Section 7 of the DPA establishes the leadership of the NPC as consisting of one Privacy Commissioner and two Deputy Privacy Commissioners[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: The Privacy Commissioner and Deputy Privacy Commissioners are appointed for a fixed term of three (3) years to ensure their independence[cite: 1].
items.question_text: What is the standard term length for the Privacy Commissioner and Deputy Privacy Commissioners?
items.correct_answer: Three (3) years
items.explanation: The Commissioners serve a term of three years, which may be reappointed for one additional term[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: The NPC exercises Quasi-Legislative (Rule-Making) Power when it drafts the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR), issues Circulars, and publishes advisories[cite: 1].
items.question_text: Which power of the NPC allows it to issue the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) and other administrative circulars?
items.correct_answer: Quasi-Legislative (Rule-Making) Power
items.explanation: Rule-making functions, such as drafting the IRR and Circulars, are classified under the NPC's Quasi-Legislative power[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: The NPC exercises Quasi-Judicial (Adjudicatory) power when it receives complaints, institutes investigations, and issues cease and desist orders for severe violations[cite: 1].
items.question_text: Which power enables the NPC to investigate complaints and issue Cease and Desist Orders against violators?
items.correct_answer: Quasi-Judicial (Adjudicatory) Power
items.explanation: Handling complaints, investigations, and issuing enforcement orders are exercises of the NPC's Quasi-Judicial power[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: Personal information processed exclusively for journalistic, artistic, literary, or research purposes is excluded from the DPA to protect freedom of expression[cite: 1].
items.question_text: Under the DPA, processing personal data is explicitly excluded from the law's strict rules if it is done exclusively for what purpose?
options: Journalistic, artistic, literary, or research purposes
items.correct_answer: Journalistic, artistic, literary, or research purposes
items.explanation: The DPA excludes processing for journalistic, artistic, literary, or research purposes to balance privacy rights with free expression and public interest[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: Information about government officers relating to their official position, title, functions, and salary grade is excluded from DPA protection to maintain transparency[cite: 1].
items.question_text: Which of the following types of information is explicitly excluded from the protection of the Data Privacy Act to ensure public transparency?
options: The personal home address of a private citizen
Information about a government official's position, title, and salary grade
The medical records of a hospital patient
The private text messages of a corporate employee
items.correct_answer: Information about a government official's position, title, and salary grade
items.explanation: Information relating to the official functions and salary range of government employees is a matter of public concern and is excluded from the DPA[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: Processing personal information exclusively for personal, family, or household affairs is excluded from the DPA[cite: 1].
items.question_text: If a person keeps a personal diary or address book strictly for family and household affairs, does the Data Privacy Act apply?
options: Yes, all personal lists are strictly regulated.
No, processing exclusively for personal, family, or household affairs is exempt from the DPA.
Yes, but only if they have more than 100 contacts.
No, unless they use a computer to type the diary.
items.correct_answer: No, processing exclusively for personal, family, or household affairs is exempt from the DPA.
items.explanation: Section 3(h) of the DPA explicitly excludes individuals processing data strictly in connection with personal, family, or household affairs[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: Information necessary for banks and financial institutions to comply with the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) is excluded from the DPA[cite: 1].
items.question_text: Information processed by financial institutions is excluded from the DPA if it is necessary to comply with which specific law?
options: The Consumer Act of the Philippines
items.correct_answer: The Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA)
items.explanation: To combat financial crimes, Section 4 of the DPA excludes information necessary for banks to comply with AMLA[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: Information relating to individuals performing services under contract for a government institution is excluded from the DPA to ensure accountability in public spending[cite: 1].
items.question_text: Is the name and contract details of a private individual performing services for a government agency protected from public disclosure under the DPA?
options: Yes, all contractor data is completely confidential.
No, information relating to individuals performing services under a government contract is excluded from the DPA.
Yes, unless the contract is for a foreign government.
No, but the individual must give consent first.
items.correct_answer: No, information relating to individuals performing services under a government contract is excluded from the DPA.
items.explanation: Section 4(b) removes DPA protections for information relating to the terms of the contract and the services performed by government contractors[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: The NPC was created specifically to administer, implement, and monitor compliance with the provisions of the Data Privacy Act[cite: 1].
items.question_text: What is the primary legal mandate of the National Privacy Commission (NPC)?
options: To prosecute internet scammers in regular courts
To issue national ID cards to all citizens
To administer and implement the provisions of the Data Privacy Act
To manage the social media accounts of government officials
items.correct_answer: To administer and implement the provisions of the Data Privacy Act
items.explanation: The NPC was established under RA 10173 to serve as the primary regulatory body to enforce the Data Privacy Act[cite: 1].
